# Mapdamage 2 running on bash

## software used to assess the DNA damage of our museum adder samples

```bash

conda create -n mapdamage_test
#this creates the environment labelled angsd_test using conda within your home space
 

conda install bioconda::mapdamage2
#installs the angsd package

conda --help
#gives a list of conda functionalities and commands

conda activate mapdamage_test
#actiates the conda environment called mapdamage_test 

# create slurm script to run mapdamage software

#!/bin/bash
###
#job name
#SBATCH --job-name=mapdamageS22

#job stdoutput file
#SBATCH --output=/scratch/SCWF00035/people/b.dvb25fyc_david/BEARCAVE2/mapeddamageres/mapdamageS22%J
#job stderror file
#SBATCH --error=/scratch/SCWF00035/people/b.dvb25fyc_david/BEARCAVE2/mapeddamageres/mapdamageS22%J
#maximum job time in D-HH:MM
#SBATCH --time=0-04:00
#number of nodes (axel almost never needs more than 1)
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#number of parallel processes (tasks) in CPU'S
#SBATCH --ntasks=10
#memory in Gb
#SBATCH --mem=15G
#assign account
#SBATCH --account=SCWF00035_a_barlow_33

module purge
module load Anaconda3/2025.06-1
source activate mapdamage_test

ref='/scratch/SCWF00035/BEARCAVE0/refgenomes/rVipBer3/GCA_964194415.1_newheaders.fa'

bam='/scratch/SCWF00035/BEARCAVE0/mappedrVipBer3_aln/46y+S22_1895_ber_rVipBer3_7.58190.bam'

mapDamage -i $bam -r $ref --no-stats

# re-run for all museum samples in the study, change bam file pathway each time to relevant sample bam
```
